The investigated samples were GaN thin layers with embedded γ'-Ga₄₋ₓFeₓN nanocrystals fabricated by metal organic vapor phase epitaxy.
The nanocrystals size varied from (50±20)nm to (20±8)nm in the layer plane and (17±8)nm along the c-growth direction.
The nanocrystal density ranged from 3.9 x 10⁹ NC/cm² to 15.0 x 10⁹ NC/cm², tunable by the amount of Ga provided during growth.
The DAFS analysis showed that Ga atoms preferentially occupy the 3c Wyckoff sites in the fcc structure of the nanocrystals.
The maximum Ga occupancy in the 3c sites of the nanocrystals was around 30%.
The lattice parameter of the nanocrystals along the c-growth direction increased with increasing Ga content, reaching values comparable or larger than those reported for γ'-GaFe₃N powders.
The Curie temperature of the nanocrystals ranged from 450K to 500K, decreasing with increasing Ga content in the 3c sites.
The normalized saturation magnetization of the nanocrystals decreased with increasing Ga content in the 3c sites.

The combination of AXD and DAFS allowed the authors to isolate the contribution of Ga in the nanocrystals, overcoming the challenge of the presence of Ga in the surrounding GaN matrix and capping layer.
The authors found that the inclusion of Ga in the 3c sites does not affect the ferromagnetic character and magnetization values of the nanocrystals up to 30% Ga content.

The results demonstrate the potential of the DAFS method for unraveling the local structure of similar magnetic phase-separated systems even when the nanocrystals and the surrounding matrix contain the same absorber under investigation.
The samples were grown on a 1 μm thick GaN buffer layer deposited on a c-plane sapphire (Al₂O₃) substrate.
A 30 nm GaN nucleation layer was deposited to compensate the lattice mismatch between the substrate and buffer.
The GaN capping layer thickness ranged from 40 nm to 300 nm to prevent the formation of α-Fe nanocrystals at the sample surface.
The 2θ-ω HRXRD scans showed an additional diffraction peak assigned to the (200) diffraction planes of the γ'-Ga₄₋ₓFeₓN nanocrystals.
